# ci-artifact-container

**Publish the container images a revision built to a registry.**

A forge-ci `artifact` engine.

## Why it exists

A container is an artifact like a binary, so it is built by a build stage and
published by a release stage. This is the release half: it filters the artifacts
the runs produced down to the containers, and pushes each layout under the version
the core decided.

It computes no version and reads no tag line. Two authorities over one number is
how every member of a workspace drifted onto a version line of its own.

## Tools

| Tool | Does |
|---|---|
| `declare` | Report the resources this release needs. It needs none. |
| `publish` | Push every container image the revision built, under the version. |

## By hand

```sh
echo '{"revision":"3dd48e96ed7e","version":"v0.50.0","artifacts":[{"name":"toolchain","type":"container","location":"file:///w/build/images/toolchain.oci"}],"spec":{"image":"ghcr.io/owner/forge"}}' \
  | ci-artifact-container publish
```

## In a pipeline

```yaml
engines:
  - alias: my-artifact
    type: artifact
    engine: "forge://github.com/alexandremahdhaoui/forge-ci/cmd/ci-artifact-container@v0.1.0"
    manager: local
    spec:
      image: <string>
      movingTags: <list of strings>
      labels: <map of string to string>
      tokenEnv: <string>
```

## Worth knowing

A dirty revision is refused. It was never proven, so publishing it ships
something nobody can reproduce.

What publishes: every artifact whose type is container. Filtering on the type is
what keeps a binary out of the registry and a container off the upload path. A
stage that built no container fails the release rather than publishing nothing
quietly, because a tag silently left pointing at last week's image is worse than
a red build.

The tag is the version, with the factory's prefix in front of it when it has one.
Nothing else is pinnable: spec.movingTags names convenience tags like "latest"
that point at the same index and move on every release.

There is no daemon, no CLI and no docker login. go-containerregistry speaks the
registry HTTP API directly and the auth handshake is part of the push, with the
token named by spec.tokenEnv - GITHUB_TOKEN by default, which GitHub Actions
injects, so there is no secret to create, seal or rotate. A job that publishes
needs permissions: packages: write.

With no token the requests go out anonymous rather than reading the machine's
docker config, because an engine that silently picks up whatever credential is
lying around publishes to somewhere nobody named.
